items.name: credentials/listAccounts
items.direction: Plugin → Matrix Agent → Nexus `GET /api/v1/executa/credentials/accounts` → platform credential store
items.summary:
Enumerate the accounts the user has authorized for one platform provider — **metadata only, never tokens**. A user may connect several accounts of the same provider (e.g. work + personal Gmail) on `/settings/authorizations`; exactly one per provider is the **default** (`is_default: true`), which is what classic `context.credentials` injection resolves to. Use this to render/describe an account choice, resolve an email to an `account_id`, or feed `credentials/getToken`.

**Pre-requisites** (both required):
1. **Manifest declaration.** Your `credentials[]` block declares at least one name that maps to an **OAuth** provider through the platform's `credential_mapping` (e.g. `GOOGLE_ACCESS_TOKEN` → `google`). API-key providers (GitHub / Notion / Slack) have no account dimension and never unlock this surface.
2. **Per-invoke token.** The host minted a `credentials_token` for this invoke (automatic when #1 holds — no user grant, no `host_capabilities` entry; the user already authorized the provider platform-wide). Missing → `CREDENTIALS_NOT_GRANTED` (-32061).

**Auth chain.** The plugin never holds a long-lived secret: the Agent reads the per-invoke `credentials_token` (aud=`executa-credentials`, ~10 min TTL, claims: `user_id`, `executa_tool_id`, `tool_invoke_id`, `providers[]`) from `ctx` and forwards to Nexus with `Authorization: Bearer <credentials_token>`; Nexus re-checks the requested `provider` against the token's `providers` claim on every request.
items.signature: CredentialsClient.list_accounts(*, provider: str, timeout: float = 30.0) -> dict

params.name: provider
params.summary: Platform provider id (e.g. `"google"`, `"twitter"`). Must be covered by the invoke's `credentials_token` `providers` claim — i.e. one of the OAuth providers your declared credential names map to.
notes: Provider ids are the keys of the platform registry `src/services/credential_providers.py` — NOT credential names.
A provider outside the claim fails with `CREDENTIALS_NOT_GRANTED` (-32061) carrying the nexus code `APP_NOT_GRANTED`.

returns.desc:
`{"accounts": [{account_id, email, label, is_default, status, scopes}]}`.

- `account_id` is the stable per-account key (= the provider's user id) — pass it to `credentials/getToken`.
- Exactly one account per provider has `is_default: true` (service-maintained invariant; the user can change it per row on the authorizations page).
- `status ∈ {active, expired, revoked, error}` — anything but `active` means `getToken` for that account will fail until the user reconnects; surface it instead of retrying.
- **Never contains tokens** — safe to echo into tool output.

errors.name: CREDENTIALS_NOT_GRANTED
errors.desc: `credentials_token` missing from ctx (manifest declares no OAuth-mapped credential name) or `provider` not covered by the token's `providers` claim.

errors.name: CREDENTIALS_INVALID_REQUEST
errors.desc: `provider` missing/empty or params not an object. Raised Agent-side before any HTTP.

errors.name: CREDENTIALS_UPSTREAM
errors.desc: Nexus unreachable / non-2xx without a mapped error envelope. `subcall_timeout` error_name when the per-call budget (`_clientTimeoutS`, cap 60 s) elapses.

errors.name: CREDENTIALS_TIMEOUT (SDK-local)
errors.desc: The SDK-side `await` timed out before the host replied.

limitations: OAuth providers only — API-key providers have no account dimension.
Executa channel gating is manifest-declaration only; the per-app `credentials_grant` gate applies to the iframe HOST API channel (`anna.credentials.*`), not here.
Not served by the offline dev harness — requires a real host (`anna-app dev` against a logged-in Agent).
items.example:
from executa_sdk import CredentialsClient, CredentialsError

creds = CredentialsClient()
# register with make_response_router(...) alongside your other clients

async def pick_account(email: str | None) -> str | None:
    out = await creds.list_accounts(provider="google")
    accounts = out["accounts"]
    if email:
        match = [a for a in accounts if (a["email"] or "").lower() == email.lower()]
        return match[0]["account_id"] if match else None
    return None  # None → getToken uses the default account

items.name: credentials/getToken
items.direction: Plugin → Matrix Agent → Nexus `POST /api/v1/executa/credentials/token` → per-row refresh state machine
items.summary:
Exchange a **short-lived access token** for one of the user's authorized accounts. Omit `account_id` for the default account — which makes this a superset of classic `context.credentials` injection: same token, but fetched on demand and per account.

Internally rides the platform's per-credential-row refresh state machine: an expired-but-refreshable token is refreshed transparently before return (each connected account refreshes independently); a dead credential (revoked, refresh_token invalid) fails with `CREDENTIALS_NOT_GRANTED` and the user must reconnect on `/settings/authorizations`.

**Multi-account tools.** Declare `"multi_account": true` on a tool in your manifest and the platform injects an optional LLM-visible `account` argument ("Target account email or id; omit for default") into its args schema. The value arrives as a plain tool argument — resolve emails via `credentials/listAccounts`, then pass the `account_id` here.

**Red lines.** Per-call short-lived tokens (audit-friendly); `refresh_token` never crosses this channel; mask tokens before they can land in tool output or chat transcripts (see `examples/anna-app-credentials-demo`'s `token_info`).
items.signature: CredentialsClient.get_token(*, provider: str, account_id: str | None = None, timeout: float = 30.0) -> dict

params.name: provider
params.summary: Platform provider id — same semantics and gating as `credentials/listAccounts`.

params.name: account_id
params.summary: Stable account key from `credentials/listAccounts` (`accounts[].account_id`). Emails are NOT accepted here — resolve them via `listAccounts` first.
notes: Unknown `account_id` → `CREDENTIALS_NOT_GRANTED` (-32061) with an explanatory message — treat as "ask the user / re-list", not retry.

returns.desc:
`{"access_token": str, "account_id": str, "expires_at": str|null}`.

- `account_id` echoes the account that actually served the token (resolved default included) — log it for audit, prefer it over your input.
- `expires_at` is ISO-8601 or null when the provider didn't report an expiry. Don't cache beyond it; just call again — refresh is the platform's job.
- The token is a live provider credential (e.g. a Google `ya29.…`). Use it in the provider API call and drop it; never store, never print unmasked.

errors.name: CREDENTIALS_NOT_GRANTED
errors.desc: Token missing / provider not covered / unknown account / credential unusable (expired terminal, revoked — nexus code `APP_NOT_GRANTED` with a reconnect hint in the message).

errors.name: CREDENTIALS_UPSTREAM
errors.desc: Nexus unreachable / unmapped upstream failure; `subcall_timeout` on budget overrun.

limitations: One token per call — batch flows should reuse the token until `expires_at` rather than calling per request.
No scope narrowing per call: the token carries whatever scopes the user granted the platform at connect time (`accounts[].scopes`).
Not served by the offline dev harness.
